'''Gustaf Hjalmar Eneström''' (5 September 1852 – 10 June 1923) was a [[Swedish people|Swedish]] [[mathematician]], [[statistician]] and [[historian]] of mathematics known for introducing the Eneström index, which is used to identify [[Euler]]'s writings. Most historical scholars refer to the works of Euler by their Eneström index.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://eulerarchive.maa.org/index/enestrom.html|title=The Eneström Index|last=|first=|date=|website=The Euler Archive|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403182845/http://eulerarchive.maa.org/index/enestrom.html|archive-date=2018-04-03|access-date=2017-10-15|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Eneström received a [[Bachelor of Science]] (''filosofie kandidat'') degree from [[Uppsala university]] in 1871, received a position at [[Uppsala University Library]] in 1875, and at the [[National Library of Sweden]] in 1879.

From 1884 to 1914, he was the publisher of the mathematical-historical journal ''[[Bibliotheca Mathematica]]'', which he had founded and partially funded with his own means. Concerning the history of mathematics, he was known as critical to [[Moritz Cantor]].

With [[Soichi Kakeya]], he is known for the [[Eneström-Kakeya theorem]]<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Gardner | first1=Robert Bentley
| date=1997
| title=Some generalizations of the Eneström-Kakeya Theorem
| journal=[[Acta Mathematica Hungarica]]
| volume=74
| issue=1–2
| pages=125–134
| doi=10.1007/BF02697881| s2cid=120493761
}}</ref> which determines an [[annulus (mathematics)|annulus]] containing the roots of a real [[polynomial]]. Specifically, it states that for an <math>n</math>-degree polynomial <math>P(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^n a_{k} z^{k}</math> with a complex variable <math>z</math> and real coefficients satisfying <math>0 \le a_0 \le a_1 \le \cdots \le a_n</math>, all zeros of <math>P(z)</math> lie within the disk <math>|z| \le 1</math>.

In 1923 [[George Sarton]] wrote, "No one has done more for the sound development of our studies". Sarton went on: "the very presence of Eneström obliged every scholar devoting himself to the [[history of mathematics]] to increase his circumspection and improve his work."<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Sarton | first1=George
| date=1923
| title=Notes and Correspondence–For Gustav Eneström's Seventy-First Anniversary
| journal=[[Isis (journal)|Isis]]
| volume=5
| issue=2
| pages=421
| doi=10.1086/358166 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

Eneström has also developed an election method similar to [[Phragmen's voting rules]].<ref>{{Cite arXiv |eprint=1907.10590 |last1=Camps |first1=Rosa |last2=Mora |first2=Xavier |last3=Saumell |first3=Laia |title=The method of Eneström and Phragmén for parliamentary elections by means of approval voting |date=2019 |class=econ.TH }}</ref>
